examDifficulty.heading: Is the Nonprofit Cloud Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam asks you to apply Salesforce knowledge to nonprofit scenarios. Practice choosing a configuration or troubleshooting approach for a stated need.
bullets: 65% passing score: build a margin above the minimum before booking.
Scenario-based choices: expect questions that test when to use Nonprofit Data Model, NPSP Configuration, or Donation Management.
Practice matters. Build a sample donor household, record a gift, and follow its payment and reporting data.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Before booking, practice a complete nonprofit workflow: create a constituent, record a donation, track a payment, and report on fundraising results. Aim for 75% or more on timed practice.

examFormat.heading: Nonprofit Cloud Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Use timed practice sets to prepare for the Nonprofit Cloud exam and review the topics you find difficult.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Expect nonprofit scenarios about gifts, households, grant applications, and service delivery. Identify the record or process that matches the organization’s goal.
bestWayToPass: Trace a constituent: Follow a person from a household or organization relationship through donations and program participation.
Practice gift entry: Compare a one-time gift, recurring donation, payment, in-kind gift, and soft credit.
Review program and grant records: Learn how services, grant requirements, and outcomes are tracked.
Build nonprofit reports: Practice donor retention, campaign results, gift summaries, and program measures.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers implementing Salesforce for nonprofits, including the NPSP data model, fundraising with donations and recurring giving, program management, grant tracking, and impact reporting. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 65% pass mark, weighted towards Agentforce Nonprofit Feature Configuration (35%) and Solution Design (32%).

keyConcepts.h2: Nonprofit Cloud Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: NPSP Core Data Model: Households and Affiliations
blocks.body: NPSP uses household Accounts to group related Contacts. Affiliations connect people to organizations, such as employers or boards. Nonprofit Cloud and NPSP use different product models, so check which solution an organization uses before choosing its data design.

blocks.heading: Fundraising: Opportunities, Payments, and Recurring Donations
blocks.body: In NPSP, an Opportunity can represent a gift, and payment records can track amounts received. Recurring Donations can generate a series of Opportunities. Soft Credits give recognition to someone other than the primary donor. Configure these records to match fundraising practices.

blocks.heading: Program Management: Services and Deliveries
blocks.body: The Program Management Module tracks participation and services. A Program describes an offering, a Program Engagement links a participant to it, and a Service Delivery records a service provided. Use these records to report on activity and outcomes.

blocks.heading: Grant Management: Funds and Allocations
blocks.body: General Accounting Units (GAUs) represent funds or purposes, and allocations can divide a gift among them. Grant management records can track applications, awards and funder requirements. Choose a structure that supports reporting on restricted funds.

blocks.heading: Reporting and Impact Measurement
blocks.body: Fundraising reports can show donor retention, gift size and changes in giving over time. Program reports can show services delivered and outcomes. Choose measures that help the organization report to its board, funders and other stakeholders. [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant) can support this analysis.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Study how Nonprofit Cloud supports fundraising and program work, and compare its data model with other Salesforce implementations.

blocks.heading: NPSP Household Account Model
blocks.body: For an NPSP household, review how Contacts are grouped and how duplicate records and shared giving affect reports.

blocks.heading: Gift Entry & Payment Processing
blocks.body: Trace a gift from entry through payment and credit. Check the capabilities of the specific nonprofit product in the scenario.

blocks.heading: Relationships & Affiliations
blocks.body: Use Relationships for connections between people and Affiliations for a person’s connection to an organization.

blocks.heading: Program Management
blocks.body: In PMM, distinguish the program, a participant’s engagement and each service delivery before designing reports.

blocks.heading: TDTM (Table-Driven Trigger Management)
blocks.body: In NPSP, review TDTM handler configuration when troubleshooting managed trigger behavior.

sampleQuestions.question: Which data model can a nonprofit use to manage donations in Salesforce?
options: The Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP) data model.
Custom objects with no standard Salesforce records.
The standard Account object by itself.
A Campaign Member record for each gift.
sampleQuestions.explanation: NPSP provides a nonprofit data model for fundraising records such as donations.
whyWrong: This is the nonprofit data model used for donation records.
A custom-only model does not use the nonprofit data model described.
Accounts can relate donors and organizations, but they do not track gifts on their own.

sampleQuestions.question: What do Household Accounts represent in NPSP?
options: Volunteer shifts for community events.
Foundation grant applications.
Companies that make corporate gifts through a matching programme.
Groups of individual Contacts who are part of one household.
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Household Account groups related individual Contacts and supports household-level relationship tracking.
whyWrong: Volunteer shifts are tracked with volunteer management records.
Grant applications are tracked separately from households.
A corporate donor is generally represented as an organization Account.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature can record a donation of goods or services instead of cash?
options: A standard cash Opportunity with no extra details.
Gift Entry, which only enters cash donations.
In-Kind Gift fields on the Opportunity.
A Campaign Member record.
sampleQuestions.explanation: In-Kind Gift fields on an Opportunity can record non-cash donations.
whyWrong: A cash Opportunity alone does not capture the in-kind details.
Gift Entry supports gift entry, but this option does not identify the in-kind fields.
This is the option used to track donated goods or services.

sampleQuestions.question: What is an Engagement Plan used for in NPSP?
options: Automating marketing emails.
Scheduling fundraising events and their volunteer shifts.
Sending email campaigns.
Creating task templates for donor follow-up.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Engagement Plans create task templates for donor stewardship and follow-up.
whyWrong: Marketing automation is a separate purpose.
Event management is not the purpose of Engagement Plans.
An email campaign does not create the donor task plan described.

sampleQuestions.question: How can NPSP manage a recurring donation?
options: Use a Recurring Donation record that can generate installment Opportunities.
Enter a new donation manually each month.
Use only standard Salesforce scheduling.
Track it only in an external payment processor, with nothing stored in Salesforce.
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Recurring Donation record can create Opportunities on the selected schedule.
whyWrong: This is the NPSP feature designed for scheduled gifts.
Manual entry is not needed for a configured recurring donation.
Standard scheduling alone does not manage the donation records.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Soft Credit record?
options: A donated item or service.
A pledge that has been promised but has not yet been paid.
Recognition for someone who helped influence a gift.
A refunded payment.
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Soft Credit recognizes a person or organization that influenced a donation without making the primary gift.
whyWrong: An in-kind gift is a non-cash donation.
A pledge is a promise to give, not a Soft Credit.
A refund is handled as a payment adjustment.

sampleQuestions.question: Which NPSP feature supports tribute or memorial gifts?
options: Tribute and memorial fields and related processes.
A Household Account by itself.
A standard Opportunity with no tribute information.
A Campaign record only.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tribute and memorial fields let the organization record gifts made in someone’s honor or memory.
whyWrong: A Household Account does not record tribute details on its own.
An Opportunity may hold a gift, but it needs tribute information.
A Campaign may organize outreach but does not record tribute details by itself.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an Affiliation record link?
options: A Contact to a Campaign only.
A donation to its payment only.
A Contact to an organization, such as an employer or school.
Two Household Accounts that happen to share one mailing address.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Affiliations connect a Contact with an organization, such as an employer or school.
whyWrong: Campaign membership is handled with Campaign Member records.
Payment records are linked to gifts, not Affiliations.
Affiliations link Contacts to organizations rather than households.

sampleQuestions.question: Which NPSP feature can track volunteer work?
options: Campaigns.
Opportunities.
Volunteer Jobs and Volunteer Hours.
Household Accounts and their members.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Volunteer Jobs and Volunteer Hours can track volunteer opportunities and completed service.
whyWrong: Campaigns are not the only volunteer tracking records.
Opportunities track gifts or grants, not volunteer hours.
Households do not track volunteer shifts by themselves.

sampleQuestions.question: What do NPSP Payment records track?
options: Campaign creation and membership.
Payments received for an Opportunity, including installments.
Household relationships.
The replacement of the Opportunity record after the gift is closed.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Payment records track amounts received against an Opportunity, such as payments toward a pledge.
whyWrong: Campaigns are managed with Campaign records.
This describes NPSP Payment records.
Households group people; they do not track payments.

sampleQuestions.question: Which records help manage nonprofit grant applications and their requirements?
options: Household Accounts alone.
Grant application, requirement, and reporting records.
A standard Opportunity alone, with no related requirement records.
Campaigns alone.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Grant management features track applications, requirements, and reporting.
whyWrong: Household Accounts do not manage grant requirements.
An Opportunity may represent a grant but does not cover all grant requirements by itself.
Campaigns can organize outreach but do not manage grant compliance alone.

sampleQuestions.question: What can the NPSP Forecast object support?
options: Inventory planning.
Fundraising budget and revenue forecasts.
Campaign email delivery.
Sales forecasts for commercial product lines.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Forecast records can support fundraising budget and revenue planning.
whyWrong: Inventory planning is not the purpose of this object.
Campaign email delivery uses marketing features.
This is not limited to sales forecasting.

sampleQuestions.question: Which report is useful to a nonprofit fundraising team?
options: Donor retention, campaign results, and gift totals.
Open customer support Cases grouped by product and priority.
Sales pipeline only.
Product sales only.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Nonprofit teams often track donor retention, campaign performance, and gift totals.
whyWrong: Support Cases do not measure fundraising results.
Sales pipeline reporting is not the nonprofit need described.
Product sales reports do not summarize donations.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the Primary Affiliation on a Contact used for?
options: Tracking donations only.
Identifying the Contact’s main organization, such as an employer.
Managing Campaign membership.
Replacing the Contact’s Household Account with the employer’s Account.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Primary Affiliation marks a Contact’s main relationship to an organization, such as an employer.
whyWrong: Gift records track donations.
This is the purpose of Primary Affiliation.
Campaign membership is tracked separately.

sampleQuestions.question: Which systems are commonly connected to a nonprofit Salesforce org?
options: Payment, fundraising, and accounting systems.
Slack.
Marketing Cloud, with no other system connected.
CPQ.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Nonprofits often connect payment processing, fundraising tools, and accounting systems.
whyWrong: Slack can support collaboration but is not the only common nonprofit integration.
Marketing tools may be used, but they do not cover the integration needs described.
CPQ is not the common integration set described here.
